links.outcome: LLM rating reliability across repeated runs, temperature settings and prompting styles
links.effect: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk); lower temperatures consistently improved reliability and accuracy.
links.quote: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk), while few-shot prompting showed best human-AI agreement for very high risk (α=0.78, 95% CI: [0.67-0.89]) and strongest classification performance (balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71).

links.outcome: reliability across temperature and prompt configurations
links.effect: Configuration strongly influenced reliability; zero-shot temperature 0 had α=1.00 for high and very high risk.
links.quote: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk), while few-shot prompting showed best human-AI agreement for very high risk (α=0.78, 95% CI: [0.67-0.89]) and strongest classification performance (balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71).

links.outcome: recognition of suicide-risk categories and clinical items
links.effect: Best very-high-risk agreement α=0.78; balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71; critical clinical items had poor validity.
links.quote: However, critical clinical items showed poor validity.

links.outcome: LLM accuracy against human expert suicide-risk ratings
links.effect: Best very-high-risk agreement α=0.78; strongest balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71; item performance inconsistent.
links.quote: However, inconsistent clinical item performance and only moderate to-human agreement limit LLMs to initial screening rather than detailed assessment, requiring careful parameter control and validation.
